# Organic chemistry and molecular structure (`organic_structure_theory`)

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from techtree/core/chemistry.yaml — do not edit -->

- Category: Chemistry (`chemistry`)
- Deps: needs molecules_mole_concept; helped by distillation
- Core idea: The substances of living things are built mainly of carbon, hydrogen, oxygen and nitrogen and obey the same laws as minerals; no life force is needed to make them. Each carbon atom forms four bonds and carbon atoms link into chains and rings, so a substance is defined not just by which atoms it contains but by how they are connected: two substances with the same composition can differ (isomers). Benzene is a ring of six carbons. Drawing the structure lets the chemist plan how to build a wanted molecule step by step.
- Pitfalls:
  - The legend that Wöhler's urea of 1828 ended vitalism overnight; the change took decades.
  - Treating formulae as pictures of flat things; carbon with four single bonds is approximately tetrahedral; double-bonded carbon is usually planar.
  - Taking Kekulé's dream of the snake as history; he told it 25 years later.
  - 'Organic' here means carbon chemistry, not natural or wholesome.
- History: europe: 1828 Wöhler makes urea; 1831 Liebig's combustion analysis; 1858 Kekulé and Couper, tetravalent carbon and chains; 1861 Butlerov, 'chemical structure'; 1865 Kekulé's benzene ring; 1874 van 't Hoff and Le Bel, tetrahedral carbon
- Read:
  - Alan J. Rocke, Image and Reality: Kekulé, Kopp, and the Scientific Imagination (2010)
  - William H. Brock, The Fontana History of Chemistry (1992)
